overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law at its September 30 meeting by holding an executive session for employee performance reviews (not a permitted purpose) and by failing to follow the entry procedure; it must release the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission entered executive session at its Sept 30 meeting for an improper purpose, namely to conduct employee evaluations.
allegations.key_passage: The entire executive session was a discussion of professional competence and performance, and thus it was not appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint concerned the Sept 30 executive session; the minutes showed no roll call vote to enter and no statutory purpose stated by the Chair.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes do not reflect a roll call vote to enter into executive session, nor did the Chair state which of the ten executive session purposes the Commission sought to invoke to justify the executive session.

allegations.summary: The Commission was withholding the minutes of the Sept 30 executive session; the AG addressed whether withholding remains permitted.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law and may not continue to withhold the minutes of the September 30 executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; the Commission is cautioned that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
Publicly release the minutes of the Commission's September 30 executive session, without redaction, at a meeting within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter.
Each member of the Commission must review the Attorney General's training video on executive sessions and certify compliance within 30 days of receipt of the determination.
remedy_passage: Publicly release the minutes of the Commission's September 30 executive session, without redaction. This must occur at a meeting within thirty (30) days of the Commission's receipt of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
